title: Coproduct preservation follows from copower preservation
statement: Let C be a category with zero morphisms, D any category, I a set, and F : C → D a functor. Suppose both C and D have all I-indexed coproducts. If F preserves the coproduct of the constant I-indexed family on S for every object S of C, then F preserves every I-indexed coproduct. F need not be additive or preserve zero morphisms.

source.place: Elementary arrow-retract argument written by V3; uses Mathlib MorphismProperty.of_retract and coproduct comparisons

proof.text: For any family K_i let S be its coproduct. Let j_i : K_i → S be its coprojection and p_i : S → K_i be the map equal to the identity on summand i and zero on all others. The coproduct equations give j_i followed by p_i equal to the identity.

The arrows sigmaComparison F K and sigmaComparison F (constant S) form an arrow retract. Its source maps are coproducts of F(j_i) and F(p_i); its target maps are F of the coproducts of j_i and p_i. Naturality of sigmaComparison gives the two commuting squares. Functoriality and j_i p_i = id give the retraction identities.

The constant-family comparison is invertible by the hypothesis. Isomorphisms are stable under arrow retracts, so sigmaComparison F K is invertible. Apply PreservesCoproduct.of_iso_comparison and preservesColimitsOfShape_of_discrete. No zero-preservation of F was used. If I is empty the same comparison retraction is the identity.
